correctness.rationale: All formulas are algebraically explicit for integer d>=2 and real a>=1. The sphere+cone radial profile is exact; cone-support and concave radial-gap inequalities prove John feasibility, while an exact concave quadratic proves Löwner feasibility for every spherical latitude. Pole-plus-regular-simplex contacts give explicit positive normalized first and second moment identities, proving global uniqueness by classical extremal ellipsoid theorems. The volume Taylor expansion is checked analytically. Independent code-style numerical checks across 320 cases corroborate, but finite checks are not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: A canonical minimal nonsymmetric perturbation of the Euclidean ball has both extremal-volume ellipsoids classified for all spike sizes and dimensions. The exact surprising invariance of the John ellipsoid for all a<=d, sharp change beyond a=d, and quadratic onset are nontrivial geometric consequences of the global extremal problems, not arbitrary parameter samples. The distinct enclosing response and explicit contact measures make the result useful for convex-body approximation and sharpness examples.
